```{r}
#| message: false

library(faux)
library(tidyverse)
library(lme4)
```

## Introduction

This blog post is intended to clarify the differences between **nested** and **crossed** data and how each should be analysed using mixed-effects models. It serves not only as a personal reference but also as a resource that I can share with students to help them understand these concepts. As usual, one of the best ways to understand a statistical concept is to simulate data.

## Nested

Data are nested when observations are grouped within larger units, such that obervations belonging to the same group may be correlated. For example, students may be grouped within classes, or patients treated may be treated by the same doctor. In these examples, students are nested within classes, and patients are nested within doctors. The students and patients are the lower-level observational units, whereas classes and doctors are the higher-level grouping units. At the same time, classes may be nested within schools, and doctors within hospitals. Observations from the same group may be more similar to one another than observations from different grouos. the common entity (level 1) is the class or the doctor, and level 2 are the students or patients.

We first need to simulate the nested data.

```{r}
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Show the code"

# Define parameters
student_n = 60     # number of subjects
school_n = 10      # number of schools
class_n = 3        # number of classes
b0 = 6             # Intercept (overall mean)
b1 = 1             # Fixed effect of condition
u0_school_sd <- 1  # School random intercept SD
u0_class_sd <- 1   # Class random intercept SD
u1_class_sd <- 1   # Class random slope SD
r01_class <- 0.5   # Correlation between class intercepts and slopes
sigma_sd <- 2      # Residual SD

data <- add_random(school = school_n) |> 
  add_random(class = class_n, .nested_in = "school") |> 
  add_random(students = student_n, .nested_in = "class") |> 
  add_between("students", cond = c("A", "B")) |> 
  add_recode("cond", "cond.t", A = 0, B = 1) |> 
  add_ranef("school", u0s = u0_school_sd) |> 
  add_ranef(
    "class",
    u0i = u0_class_sd,
    u1i  = u1_class_sd,
    .cors = r01_class
  ) |> 
  add_ranef(sigma = sigma_sd) |> 
  # calculate DV
  mutate(dv = b0 + u0s + u0i + (b1 + u1i) * cond.t + sigma)

head(data, 5)
```

```{r}
lmer(dv ~ cond.t + (1|school/class), data)
```
